## Grading {#grading}

Everything is out of **100%**.

```{=html}
<table class="t" data-quarto-disable-processing="true">
<thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Weight</th><th>How</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><th>Quizzes</th><td class="big">60</td><td>Four quizzes, 20% each; your <strong>best three</strong> count. The mid-semester and end-semester exams are two of the four. No makeup for a missed quiz, for any reason.</td></tr>
<tr><th>Assignments</th><td class="big">32</td><td>Six assignments, done in groups of three, with variable weights (for example 10% or 12%). Some involve pull requests to public repositories or Hugging Face Spaces-style demos.</td></tr>

</tbody></table>
```

## Assignments {#assignments}

There are six group assignments, each followed by a viva (see [Dates](#dates)). Assignment 4 is the [exposition assignment](exposition.qmd): a 4-minute video and a blog article on a tool or library, marked out of 10. All [129 team submissions](videos/videos.qmd) are online.

There are no extensions. Assignments must be written in Python, and all members of a group get the same grade.

## Assignment marks {#assignment-marks}

At the viva, the TAs first check the code against the submission; any change from the submitted code leads to a warning. They then run the code and ask questions: about 75% on the assignment itself and about 25% on the theory behind it.

```{=html}
<table class="t att" style="max-width:420px" data-quarto-disable-processing="true">
<thead><tr><th>Part</th><th>Share</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>Code runs correctly and solves the problem</td><td>50%</td></tr><tr><td>Questions on the assignment and your code</td><td>25%</td></tr><tr><td>Code quality</td><td>12.5%</td></tr><tr><td>Questions on the theory</td><td>12.5%</td></tr></tbody></table>
```

:::
